newsitem.title: USA: Lili to grow stronger as it heads toward Bahamas.
newsitem.headline: Lili to grow stronger as it heads toward Bahamas.

text.p: Hurricane Lili headed toward the central Bahamas on Friday afternoon after slamming Cuba with wind gusts of up to 115 mph (185 kmh), the National Hurricane Center said.

At 1700 EDT/2100 GMT, the center of Lili had just exited Cuba's northern coast and was located 125 miles (200 km) southwest of Andros Island in the Bahamas, forecasters said. The hurricane was travelling east-northeast at 14 mph (22 kmh) with sustained maximum winds of 90 mph (150 kmh).

"Some strengthening is possible in the next 24 hours," the hurricane center said in its 5 p.m. advisory. A hurricane warning remained in effect for the central and northwest Bahamas as well as for mainland Cuba from Matanzas province eastward to Camaguey.
Lili dumped up to 12 inches of rain in its path, causing flooding along Cuba's north coast, forecasters said.
The hurricane center also said that Lili was likely to cross the central Bahamas within the next 12 to 24 hours.
In the Bahamas, schools closed early, tourist flights were cancelled and customers crowded into food stores and gasoline stations.
